actions.description: Send one MoveRobot velocity/duration goal to the ROS 2 /move_robot action server.

inputs.description: Commanded forward velocity, mapped to the MoveRobot linear_vel_x goal field
inputs.name: linear_vel_x

inputs.description: Commanded turn rate, mapped to the MoveRobot angular_vel_z goal field
inputs.name: angular_vel_z

inputs.description: Goal duration, mapped to the MoveRobot duration goal field
inputs.name: duration

actions.name: move_robot

outputs.description: Upstream result success flag; true only when the execute loop completes normally
outputs.name: success

outputs.description: Upstream terminal result message; the cancel path sets success false
outputs.name: message

outputs.description: The linear_vel_x handed to rosbridge (the transmitted request, not a measurement)
outputs.name: sent_linear_vel_x

outputs.description: The angular_vel_z handed to rosbridge (the transmitted request, not a measurement)

outputs.description: The duration handed to rosbridge (the transmitted request, not a measurement)

facts.text: The node creates its MoveRobot action server on the relative name move_robot with a reentrant callback group.
The MoveRobot action goal declares three float64 fields: linear_vel_x, angular_vel_z and duration.
The MoveRobot action result declares a bool success and a string message.
The MoveRobot feedback declares an int64 progress value.
The goal response callback accepts every goal without inspecting its values.
The accept callback pushes every accepted goal handle onto goal_queue_.
The queue thread polls goal_queue_ at 1000 Hz and runs each popped goal's execute_callback to completion before it pops the next.
The execute loop publishes the goal's linear.x and angular.z on cmd_vel at 10 Hz and publishes a zero Twist on normal completion.
The execute loop checks is_canceling, publishes a zero Twist, sets success false and returns a canceled result.
The execute loop starts its duration from this->now().
The cancel response callback accepts every cancellation request without inspecting the goal handle.
The node constructor creates the MoveRobot action server and the joint, wheel and hand publishers; it creates no stop service and no stop action.
The bridge maps the ROS /cmd_vel topic to the Gazebo /model/my_robot/cmd_vel topic as geometry_msgs/msg/Twist in the ROS_TO_GZ direction.
The bridge configuration names /clock, /joint_states, /tf, /cmd_vel, the two camera topics and the two joint command topics.
The bringup launch starts robot_state_publisher, Gazebo, the robot spawner, ros_gz_bridge and RViz, but not the move_robot node.
The bringup launch includes ros_gz_sim gz_sim.launch.py with project_world.sdf and -r.
The bringup launch starts ros_gz_bridge parameter_bridge with the bridge configuration file.
project_world.sdf names its world empty.
The world file loads the Physics, UserCommands, SceneBroadcaster, Contact and Sensors plugins.
The DiffDrive plugin names the left and right wheel joints and sets no topic element.
The arm description loads joint position controllers on armbase_forearm_joint and forearm_hand_joint.
The README's Move Mobile Base example publishes /cmd_vel directly with ros2 topic pub -r 1.
A startup timer publishes forearm and hand joint positions through the joint command publishers; it is startup initialisation, not a stop path.
The README describes a ROS 2 Jazzy and Gazebo Harmonic mobile-manipulator simulation with a custom action server, goal queueing, progress feedback and goal cancellation.
The README's environment list names ROS 2 Jazzy and Gazebo Harmonic.
The README's install steps source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash.
The README's send_goal example targets the /move_robot action with the MoveRobot interface.
my_robot_bringup depends on ament_cmake, ros_gz_sim and ros_gz_bridge.
my_robot_bringup's license element is a TODO license declaration.
SimulationRunner composes its transport namespace as /world/ followed by the world name.
SimulationRunner advertises the control service with OnWorldControl as its callback.
OnWorldControl copies the WorldControl request into a WorldControlState and calls OnWorldControlState.
OnWorldControlState appends the control to worldControls and sets the Boolean reply to true.
ProcessWorldControl calls SetPaused with the pause flag of each queued control.
A queued control with multi_step on a paused world adds the steps and unpauses the world so that stepping can occur.
SetPaused stops the real-time stopwatch while the runner is running and the world is paused.
SetPaused stores the pause state in currentInfo.paused.
Step publishes the world statistics.
Step processes the world control messages.
The Run loop calls Step on every iteration and counts a processed iteration only while not paused.
The statistics publisher on the stats topic is limited to 10 messages per second.
PublishStats copies currentInfo.paused into the WorldStatistics message.
UpdateCurrentInfo assigns currentInfo.realTime from the real-time stopwatch on every update.
UpdateCurrentInfo advances the simulation time and the iteration count only while not paused.
The Physics system steps the physics only when not paused.
DiffDrive subscribes once, to the topic validTopic returns from a candidate list of an optional SDF topic and then /model/ followed by the model name and /cmd_vel.
validTopic returns the first candidate that AsValidTopic accepts.
DiffDrive's Configure sets enabled true.
OnCmdVel stores the Twist in targetVel while the system is enabled.
OnEnable stores the enable flag and, when disabled, zeros targetVel.
DiffDrive's PreUpdate returns early while paused.
DiffDrive's PostUpdate returns early while paused, before UpdateVelocity.
UpdateVelocity reads the stored targetVel linear x and angular z.
The joint position controller's position callback stores the commanded position.
The joint position controller's PreUpdate returns early while paused.
defaultGuiConfigFile uses gui.config unless the caller passes playback or a custom path.
The default gui.config WorldControl plugin sets play_pause, step, start_paused and use_event.
The bridge maps ros_gz_interfaces/srv/ControlWorld to a gz.msgs.WorldControl request with a gz.msgs.Boolean reply.
The ControlWorld response's success is the gz Boolean reply's data.
For a failed gz request the ControlWorld response's success is false.
The service bridge converts each ROS request and sends it with gz Request and a callback that sends the ROS response.
Node::Request with a callback requests a service using a non-blocking call.
The WorldStatistics conversion copies the gz header into the ROS header and copies paused.
ros_gz_interfaces WorldStatistics carries a header, sim_time, pause_time, real_time and the paused flag.
ControlWorld takes a WorldControl request and answers bool success.
WorldControl's fields include pause, step and multi_step.
The bridge README maps ros_gz_interfaces/msg/WorldStatistics to gz.msgs.WorldStatistics.
The bridge README maps the ros_gz_interfaces/srv/ControlWorld service to gz.msgs.WorldControl and gz.msgs.Boolean.
The bridge README's service example starts parameter_bridge with a /world/<name>/control ControlWorld argument.
Without a configured QoS profile the bridge's publisher QoS is KeepLast with the publisher queue size.
The bridge's publisher allows its deadline, depth, durability, history, liveliness and reliability QoS to be overridden.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned action terminals and world statistics that follow the wall clock; no physics step, controller loop or state hash is modelled

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free recording transport: it answers send_action_goal and cancel_action_goal for /move_robot and a canned /world/empty control service and stats topic, and runs no Gazebo Harmonic world, physics, sensors, ros_gz_bridge, differential-drive controller or action-server queue timing

the fake completes a default goal immediately and can hold one active goal only to exercise cancellation; it does not reproduce the upstream 10 Hz command loop, the 1000 Hz queue thread or the startup joint timers

the upstream action publishes geometry_msgs/Twist on cmd_vel, but the fake records no Gazebo base motion, pose, odometry or collision state; each MoveRobot receipt reports the goal it handed to rosbridge (sent_linear_vel_x, sent_angular_vel_z, sent_duration), which is the transmitted request, not a measurement
the arm command topics /forearm_joint/cmd_pos and /hand_joint/cmd_pos, /joint_states, /tf, /camera/image_raw and /camera/camera_info are not bound
the fake's canned result strings and status values are test data, not device facts, limits or a motion envelope
the action cancel path publishes a zero Twist and cancels the running goal, but queued goals remain; the fake models that queue so cancellation is not claimed as a stop

a cancel request for a queued goal is accepted at once, but the goal ends canceled only when the queue thread pops it after every goal ahead of it, so an MHS cancel waits for other clients' goals (move_robot.cpp:79-84, :95-115, :141-150); any client, including the README's ros2 topic pub example, can publish /cmd_vel directly, and the bringup launch does not start move_robot, so the operator starts it separately

the stop is the companion gz-sim world pause (WorldControl through ros_gz ControlWorld), whose reply is true for any request gz-sim queued (SimulationRunner.cc:1375-1377); it is confirmed by the E2 read-back: the fake keeps a paused flag that the control request sets after its next statistics sample and publishes /world/empty/stats every 100 ms (placeholder) while subscribed; it runs no SimulationRunner

the e-stop endpoints exist only while the operator runs ros_gz's parameter_bridge with the two arguments of operator_bridges; gazebo_bridge.yaml:1-47 names /clock, /joint_states, /tf, /cmd_vel, the camera topics and the two joint commands, and does not name /world/empty/control or /world/empty/stats; a second bridge of names the launch already bridges would be another path; without the operator bridges the control call is not answered and the read-back sees no sample, so the e-stop fails closed; the declared estop_latency_ms 1500 covers the control call (400 ms) and the read-back bound (600 ms)

the read-back's freshness is the arrival time only: the bridged WorldStatistics header is the gz header, which PublishStats does not stamp (ros_gz convert copies it, ros_gz_interfaces.cpp:840); sim_time and iterations advance only while not paused (SimulationRunner.cc:423-429); real_time is assigned from the stopwatch on every update (SimulationRunner.cc:418) and SetPaused stops that stopwatch while the runner is running and paused (SimulationRunner.cc:1282-1284), so those fields are not a freshness stamp; the bridge's default publisher QoS sets only KeepLast with the queue size (bridge_config.cpp:274-279), so its durability stays rclcpp's default, volatile, which replays no history to a late subscriber; the first sample is discarded and a burst of samples restarts the count; an operator QoS override of the stats publisher (factory.hpp:61-82) to a deeper transient-local history is not covered beyond that burst rule
the endpoints name the only world in the clone, empty (project_world.sdf:2); a launch that loads another world name does not serve these endpoints and the e-stop fails closed

the world SDF embeds no GUI plugin (project_world.sdf plugins at :8-14, and a search of the 237-line file finds no gui element); gz-sim's default GUI config is gui.config when the caller passes neither playback nor a custom path (Gui.cc:58-73), and that file's WorldControl plugin has play_pause and step (gui.config:123-141)

a live world can be unpaused or stepped by that GUI, a WorldControl multi_step (SimulationRunner.cc:1445-1452) or any client of the control service; MHS does not watch the flag after the confirmation window, and safety_status reports that retained confirmation with no fresh observation of an external unpause

no unpause is offered: DiffDrive stores the Twist in targetVel while enabled (DiffDrive.cc:637-644; Configure sets enabled true at :358) and PreUpdate and PostUpdate return while paused (:451-453, :501-505) before UpdateVelocity reads the stored linear x and angular z (:605-616), so the stored twist resumes when the world runs; OnEnable zeros targetVel only when the system is disabled (:647-656), and this package does not bind that enable topic; the joint position controller stores the commanded position (JointPositionController.cc:489-492) and its PreUpdate returns while paused (:395-397); the move_robot execute loop times the goal with this->now() (move_robot.cpp:128-131) and keeps publishing the goal Twist at 10 Hz until the duration elapses, and the clone contains no use_sim_time, so the queue keeps running on the node clock while the world is paused and overwrites a zero Twist; the bringup launch does not start move_robot; after mhs.safety.reset the world stays paused, and the operator zeros the /cmd_vel stream, stops or lets the move_robot queue drain, resets the arm targets, then unpauses outside MHS (the GUI play button or a ControlWorld request with pause false)

the deployment's gz-sim, ros_gz and gz-transport must be the pinned 8.15.0, 1.0.25 and 13.6.0 releases (ROS 2 Jazzy with Gazebo Harmonic; README.md:7, :86-88, :103); rosbridge cannot read the versions
no live ROS graph, rosbridge server, Gazebo world or hardware was contacted; the package is model-authored and remains contract_checked

safe_state.description: The world empty is paused: after the WorldControl pause two fresh stats samples, 40 ms or more apart within 600 ms, reported paused true, so the world does not step and the differential drive applies no stored twist; it is the paused flag in that window, not a measured standstill, it needs the operator-run ros_gz bridges, and no unpause is offered: the stored twist, the arm joint targets and a still-running move_robot queue act when the operator resumes the world.
